sections.thesis: Treasury yields rose as traders priced further Fed tightening after Friday's strong jobs report, lifting the 10-year yield two basis points to 4.889%.

sentences.text: Treasury yields rose as traders priced further Fed tightening after Friday's strong jobs report, lifting the 10-year yield two basis points to 4.889%.
The CME FedWatch tool put December hike odds at 82%, up from 76% on Friday, while Fed officials Barkin and Goolsbee warned about inflation.
A $58BN 3-year note sale drew a high yield of 4.627%, with the biggest tail since May.

sections.thesis: The dollar weakened as the tumble in oil prices dragged it lower, with the US Dollar Index down 0.46% to 101.81.

sentences.text: The dollar weakened as the tumble in oil prices dragged it lower, with the US Dollar Index down 0.46% to 101.81.
The Australian dollar rose 0.88% to 0.6924 on speculation that Washington and Tehran may be close to a deal, with US CPI due Tuesday.

sections.thesis: US stocks surged as investors brushed off the midterm results and last week's selloff, with the S&P 500 posting its best day in seven months.

sentences.text: US stocks surged as investors brushed off the midterm results and last week's selloff, with the S&P 500 posting its best day in seven months.
The index rose 2.3% and all 11 sectors closed higher, led by industrials as oil fell.
Nvidia fell 4.3% after its board opened a probe into whether chief executive Jensen Huang revealed sensitive information to a suspected Chinese spy.
The Nasdaq 100 rose 3.5%, recovering more than half its losses from Thursday's sell-off.

sections.thesis: Oil slumped to a 10-week low after President Trump said it was "highly unlikely" the US would renew attacks on Iran.

sentences.text: Oil slumped to a 10-week low after President Trump said it was "highly unlikely" the US would renew attacks on Iran.
Brent settled 5.9% lower at $92.57 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate 4.4% lower at $86.85, though attacks on Middle East shipping have continued.
Gold rose above $4,130 as the dollar weakened, supported by central bank buying.
